request:
Simplify existing PR input initialization

## Problem

Existing-PR Run initialization currently performs multiple layers of reconciliation before execution starts:

- read Pull Request metadata
- validate the reported head/base SHAs
- fetch the PR head ref
- verify the fetched head exactly matches the earlier API value
- fetch the base SHA
- verify that fetch again
- read Pull Request metadata a second time
- require the full selected metadata to still match the first read

This protocol is intended to detect a Pull Request changing while initialization is in progress.

That is a speculative race-handling layer around a short-lived initialization path. It adds complexity before the Run has even started.

## Expected outcome

Use the simplest input-freezing behavior needed for a Run.

Conceptually:

```text
resolve existing PR
  ↓
fetch the concrete head/base commits needed for the Run
  ↓
retain those exact commits as the Run input
  ↓
start execution
```

Do not add repeated API/fetch/API reconciliation solely to detect a hypothetical metadata race during initialization.

Once concrete commits have been fetched and retained, the Run should use those frozen commits as its input state.

If a later action needs to operate on the current Pull Request, that action can evaluate the current state at execution time.

## Context

The guiding principle is:

> Freeze the actual input once rather than building a reconciliation protocol for changes that might happen during initialization.

If a concrete incorrect-input race is observed later, address that case with the smallest necessary change.


User directive: GitWeave implements, creates a separate PR, reviews/fixes iteratively and merges only when clean. Stop on unsupported operations or permission/allowance limits and ask the user. No parent manual substitute is authorized.
